clue.text: Extortionate price for a feature of Windows that fails to start

indicators.note: failing to start means the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: a transom is the horizontal bar across a window frame

explanation.surface: A grumble that some Windows software, which won't even boot, costs an extortionate sum.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital W suggests Microsoft software; the windows are ordinary ones. 'that fails to start' drops the T from TRANSOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Money demanded for releasing a captive is a payment extorted under threat.

clue.text: One leaving Ealing to travel somewhere on the Northern Line

indicators.note: leaving says that letter departs from the place name that follows
travelling letters move about into a new order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A lone passenger leaves Ealing in west London for a station on the Northern Line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes I out of EALING, and 'to travel' rearranges what is left. The Northern Line is a London Underground line.
explanation.definitionFit: Angel is a station on the London Underground's Northern Line, in Islington.

clue.text: Keep some journals to reminisce

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Advice to keep a few old diaries so you can look back on the past.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something is to put it by for later, a straight synonym as a verb.

clue.text: Measurements satisfied a group of surveyors

parts.note: to meet a need is to satisfy it, past tense met
RICS is the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors, the UK professional body

explanation.surface: A professional body of surveyors is happy with the measurements taken.
explanation.walkthrough: RICS is the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors, Britain's professional body for surveyors.
explanation.definitionFit: Metrics are quantities measured to track performance, so measurements in a plural noun sense.

clue.text: Stand down and ease off when detectives come back inside

indicators.note: inside places the turned-round detectives within the other word

parts.note: to abate is to lessen or ease off

indicators.note: coming back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British police detectives

explanation.surface: Someone retires and relaxes once the police detectives return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come back' turns the detectives backwards, and 'inside' puts them within the word for ease off. CID is Britain's police detective branch.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch who gives up the throne steps aside formally, as an official stands down.

clue.text: A piece of Arlington covered with 100 small graves?

indicators.note: in a down clue, the coin is covered by the numeral placed on top of it

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
Arlington is in the USA, where a cent is a coin, or piece
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Arlington National Cemetery pictured as plots full of tiny graves.
explanation.walkthrough: Arlington suggests the cemetery; here it just says the coin is American. The graves are grave accents, as in à, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A grave is one kind of diacritic mark over a vowel, so several graves are examples of these marks.

clue.text: Papers overlooking the essential point of providing for people who sleep rough

indicators.note: overlooking means leaving a letter out

parts.note: a dossier is a file of papers on a subject

indicators.note: the essential point is the central letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A newspaper criticised for ignoring the core issue of support for rough sleepers.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter of 'providing' is I, which 'overlooking' removes from DOSSIERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Dosser is British slang for a homeless person who beds down outdoors or in a doss-house.

clue.text: Bus taking everybody northbound after electronic music festival in California

indicators.note: after places the turned word following the single letter

parts.note: a coach is a long-distance bus
E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: everybody means all

explanation.surface: A bus carries festival-goers north to an electronic music event in California.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'northbound' reads the word upwards; 'after' puts that turned word behind E.
explanation.definitionFit: Coachella is the annual pop and electronic music festival held in the desert near Indio, California.

clue.text: He makes films into an art form

indicators.note: to form is to shape, so these letters are moulded into a new order

explanation.surface: A director who turns cinema into art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' rearranges INTO AN ART.
explanation.definitionFit: Quentin Tarantino is an American film director, so an example of a man who makes films.

clue.text: I doubt a government gets no detailed criticism

indicators.note: de-tailed means its last letter is cut off

parts.note: stick is informal for criticism, as in taking stick

explanation.surface: Someone sceptical that a government escapes thorough criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' reads as de-tailed, losing the K of STICK. The definition is the agnostic speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unsure whether God exists might sum up their stance in two words of doubt.

clue.text: Celebs catching international flight

indicators.note: catching means holding the letter inside

parts.note: celebrities are stars

explanation.surface: Famous people board an international flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' looks like air travel; it is a flight of steps.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight is a set of steps between floors, another word for a staircase.

clue.text: I can burst in to assert commitment to a cause

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters within the other word

parts.note: to allege is to assert without proof

indicators.note: burst means the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone bursting in to declare devotion to a cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burst' turns I CAN into IANC, which goes 'in' ALLEGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Loyalty or devotion to a cause, country or leader is synonymous with being committed to it.

clue.text: A slice of honeydew with bananas

definitions.note: a plural noun naming a bunch of the fruit, for which a single collective word is used

indicators.note: a slice here is just the first letter of the melon's name

parts.note: and means with, joining two things

explanation.surface: A fruit salad: a piece of honeydew melon served with bananas.
explanation.definitionFit: A cluster of bananas growing together on the stalk is known by this collective term.

clue.text: Certain people, after initially stressing out, also cry for help

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of the two words

parts.note: and means also, adding something
SOS is the international distress signal

explanation.surface: Someone panicking and calling for help.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase stands in for unnamed persons, usually disliked ones, just as certain people does.

clue.text: The Wire … so extraordinary and different

indicators.note: extraordinary means out of the ordinary order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A viewer praising the TV drama The Wire as extraordinary and unlike anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extraordinary' rearranges THE WIRE SO. The Wire is an American TV crime drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, as in 'the facts are quite otherwise', it means not the same.

clue.text: It may be attached to an office door pane with metal screws

definitions.text: It may be attached to an office door

indicators.note: screws as a verb means twists, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Fixing a sign to a door with a pane by means of metal screws.
explanation.walkthrough: 'screws' looks like hardware but rearranges PANE and METAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A small plate bearing an occupant's name is commonly fixed to the door of an office.

clue.text: Personal photo files distributed online

indicators.note: distributed means spread around, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for electronic, used for things online

explanation.surface: Personal pictures shared around the internet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distributed' rearranges FILES; E for online is added after.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture of oneself taken with one's own phone is the definitive personal photograph.

clue.text: Young bird not entirely sheltering space from the elements?

definitions.note: an adjective phrase: something deriving from the chemical elements

indicators.note: sheltering means holding the other piece inside
not entirely means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a chick is a young bird
an em is a printer's space

explanation.surface: A fledgling partly sheltering in a space, out of the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the elements' suggests weather; the elements are chemical ones. 'not entirely' trims CHICK to CHIC, which is 'sheltering' EM.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for chemical, relating to substances built from the chemical elements.

clue.text: Stop port being besieged by a tribe

indicators.note: being besieged means surrounded, so the port goes inside

parts.note: a clan is a tribe or kinship group
Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: A port under siege from a tribe is told to halt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop' looks like a verb; it is an organ stop.
explanation.definitionFit: A clarion is a trumpet-toned organ stop, one of the knobs controlling a set of pipes.

clue.text: Bird droppings covering a dog

indicators.note: covering sets the droppings next to the a, on top of it in the word

parts.note: a cock is a male bird
poo is informal for droppings

explanation.surface: Bird mess landing on a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockapoo is a crossbreed of cocker spaniel and poodle, a type of designer dog.

clue.text: Sport clubs almost threatening to collapse

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: rickety means shaky and likely to fall apart

explanation.surface: A sports club on the verge of folding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims RICKETY to RICKET.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket is a bat-and-ball game played between two teams of eleven, an example of a sport.

clue.text: A bar opposite

definitions.meaning: a long flat-topped fixture in a shop or pub across which goods are served

explanation.definitionFit: A shop's serving surface is a bar of sorts, and acting counter to something is acting contrary to it.

clue.text: Flatbread with rice and peas for starters

indicators.note: starters are the opening letters of each of the four words

explanation.surface: A flatbread meal served with rice and peas as a side.
explanation.definitionFit: A tortilla or similar flatbread rolled around a filling is called by this name.

clue.text: Rearing birds involves a very independent set of attitudes and behaviours

parts.note: culture is a group's shared attitudes and behaviour

explanation.surface: Raising birds calls for a very independent mindset.
explanation.definitionFit: Aviculture is the keeping and breeding of birds, from Latin avis, bird.

clue.text: Tool cutting the end of paper cloth

indicators.note: cutting means removing that letter

parts.note: a trowel is a small garden or masonry tool

indicators.note: the end is the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A tool used to cut the edge of a paper cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' removes R, the end of 'paper', from TROWEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A towel is a piece of absorbent cloth for drying.

clue.text: Film college in New York

indicators.note: in places the college letter inside the rearranged city
new means made anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A film school in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New York' reads as the city, but 'New' rearranges YORK to ROKY, with C 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocky is the 1976 boxing film starring Sylvester Stallone.

clue.text: Artist taking in the Isle Of Wight Festival

indicators.note: taking in means holding the other piece inside

parts.note: Salvador Dalí was a Spanish surrealist artist
IW is the abbreviation for the Isle of Wight, an island off England's south coast

explanation.surface: A painter visiting the Isle of Wight Festival, an English rock festival.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Wight Festival is a real rock festival, but Festival is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Diwali is the Hindu festival of lights, held each autumn.

clue.text: Polish spot of ball to probe a wicket that's turning

indicators.note: probing means pushing inside
turning means the letters spin round into a new order

parts.note: O is ball-shaped

explanation.surface: Cricket: a polished ball probing a turning wicket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like shining a cricket ball; it means from Poland. 'that's turning' rearranges A WICKET, and O goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Katowice is a city in southern Poland, so a place in that country.

clue.text: Risk to the head when swallowing extremely effectual stimulant

indicators.note: swallowing means taking the letters inside

parts.note: to bet is to risk money
nut is slang for the head

indicators.note: extremely takes the outermost letters of the word

explanation.surface: A warning that some stimulant risks your head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives the first and last letters of 'effectual', which the risk and the head together are 'swallowing'.
explanation.definitionFit: The seed of the areca palm, chewed in South Asia with leaves, acts as a mild stimulant.

clue.text: Bank succeeded taking on advanced teams of relief workers

indicators.note: taking on means holding a letter inside

parts.note: to bank on is to rely on
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A bank that succeeded by hiring advanced relief teams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' looks like a noun; it is the verb, as in bank on.
explanation.definitionFit: Relays are shifts of workers who take over from one another in turn.
